naslov: You Don't Have to Do Every Good Deed Yourself to Be Rewarded for It

segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]
Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.

Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment, Lord of jinn and mankind, and blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, His beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
Dear brothers, respected congregation, in numerous verses and hadiths Islam encourages us to do good deeds and promises a great reward to the one who does them, but not only to the one who does them.
Rather, Islam also promises a reward to those who direct others to doing good deeds.
It is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that a man came to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, asking him for a mount so that he could go or travel to a certain place.

The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, did not have a mount to provide for him. Did the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, answer that man that he had none and stop there, turn around and go about his business, or did he do something more?

No, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, directed that man to another man who was able to do it. So he went to that man, got a mount, and after that informed the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, that the man had helped him.

What did the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say after that? The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “Whoever directs someone to a good deed has the same reward as the one who did that deed.” Imagine [unclear] Allah's blessings, Allah's mercy toward His servants. Sometimes you don't have to be wealthy to have the reward
of the wealthy one. It is only that you direct a person to the right address.
So if we know of some family or some person who is in need, in a difficult state, and we just direct another person who can help him, we have the reward of the person who helps.

If we know two Muslim brothers who are quarreling, and we are not particularly eloquent, nor good at reconciling, it is enough that you just direct a person who is good at reconciling two brothers, and you have a reward like the one who reconciled them.

Or anything else: if you see some obstruction to traffic on the road, it is enough that you film it and send it to those responsible, who are responsible, to the responsible institutions, as some news portals do,

and you have the reward of those who took care of it. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, promises you a reward. If we see that in some mosque, in some place, there is a useful, beautiful lecture, if we see that in some mosque the Arabic letters are being taught or something else, it is enough that you just direct one man, or two, to go there to learn the letters, and then you have the reward of their reciting the Qur'an.
We are not, dear brothers, very aware of these blessings. And you will see that people, unfortunately, share all sorts of things: with whom they had coffee, which cake they ate, what they ate.

But when it comes to these things, we have little ear for them and little motivation. And this is motivation. A reward, a great reward. Why, with so many social networks, when a person sees some khayr (good), that some good is being done, does he not share it – it takes a second.
Sometimes I think and wonder why it happens that a person does not share these good things. Either the problem is in him, or the problem lies with his company.

In both cases a person must change. If the problem is in him and he doesn't really like to share these good things, then a person must definitely ask himself: “What is wrong with me, why don't I like good to be shared, good to be heard, good to be heard about?”

If the problem is in his company, or if he shares something and expects that his company might ridicule him for it, then he must definitely change his company. He must definitely change his company. Let him distance himself from such company, because his company does not want good.

His company does not want good. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “Whoever calls to guidance,” to doing good deeds – I say, whoever calls to guidance, to doing good deeds, to worship,

or anything else beneficial, he said: “will have a reward like the reward of those who did it” – who came to that lecture, who helped their brother, who reconciled their two brothers – and he said: “nothing will be diminished from their reward.”
Nothing will be diminished from their reward. What an incentive this is, dear brothers! What motivation for us, for us believers, Muslims, especially for us who come to Jumu'ah.

And no more than ten percent of people come to Jumu'ah. And all of us, dear brothers, remember, who come here, even those who come only for Jumu'ah, we are da'is, we are callers to the truth, because whatever good we hear here in the hutba (Friday sermon), it is our obligation to convey it, to convey it to others.

I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who spread His religion, to make us among those who spread good. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us our sins and those of our parents, I ask Him, the Exalted, to help our Muslim brothers in every place, to help our brothers in Gaza, to help our brothers in Sudan, in Somalia, in every, in every place.
آمين يا رب العالمين. بارك الله لي ولكم في القرآن العظيم، ونفعني وإياكم بما فيه من الآيات والذكر الحكيم. أقول قولي هذا وأستغفر الله لي ولكم فاستغفروه إنه هو الغفور الرحيم.
